newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa well after surgical procedure.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa well after surgical procedure.

text.p: Mother Teresa underwent a successful X-ray test and surgical procedure on Friday following bouts of heart failure, an Indian clinic official said.
"Both the angiography and the angioplasty are over. She is well. It is a success," A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta, told reporters.
"I heard that she came out of the operation theatre smiling and doctors congratulated her," said Sister Prassana, a nun at Missionaries of Charity, founded by Mother Teresa.
The legendary Roman Catholic nun, 86, entered hospital on November 22 with an irregular heart-beat. She was moved to the Birla clinic on Tuesday.
Angiography is an X-ray test which, using an opaque dye, shows up any blocked arteries. Angioplasty is a surgical procedure to unblock an artery by inserting a balloon and inflating it.
Doctors earlier said Mother Teresa's condition had improved and she was feeling better.
